LITERATURE IN ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. run
   C. happiness
   D. blue

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. goes
   C. went
   D. going

3. When practising Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Charact, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Charact.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Charact.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Charact.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Charact.

4. When practising Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.

   B. Copy random text without understanding Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Literature 2.1.1 Oral Narratives: Introduction - Definition - Features - Ty.

6. When practising Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.

7. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only an action
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a describing word

8. When practising Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla.

9. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. No full stops

10. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. where is the library

----

2. C — went

3. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non - Fiction 2.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Charact.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Literature 1.1.1 Introduction to Oral Literature - Definition - Genres/ Cla.

10. C — Where is the library?

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Oral Literature 6.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry Lullabies and play songs - Form - Featu; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Poetry 6.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Language and Style: - Repetition - Refrain -; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Fiction and Non- Fiction 6.3.1 Fiction: Anthology of short stories - Features - ; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Fiction: Anthology of short stories - Features - Short stories and the history -; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
